# Specialist Dance 1.6.1 — Two Build Variants (pre-release)

Two jars, one per host. The GitHub jar keeps the bundled `specialist` dance and the `default` track; the lite jar ships without them for CurseForge and Modrinth, where you bring your own content. Jar names now state the Minecraft version, the loader and the variant.

Pre-release: the lite build has only run as a development client, and the **K** menu with nothing installed has not been seen in-game. See `ROADMAP.md`, "Patch — v1.6.1".

## Added

- The `modVariant` build property — `./gradlew build` produces the full jar, `./gradlew build -PmodVariant=lite` produces the content-less one.
- Jar names that say what they are: `specialist-dance-1.21.11-fabric-1.6.1.jar` and `specialist-dance-1.21.11-fabric_lite-1.6.1.jar`.
- `DanceRegistry.NO_DANCE` — a zero-frame `none` sentinel, so the registry still answers when nothing is installed and no caller has to null-check.
- The **Music** and **Dance** panes name the folder to drop files into when their list is empty.

## Changed

- The bundled dance and track are detected at runtime by a resource probe (`frame_000.png`, `default.ogg`) instead of assumed, so each build only offers what it actually ships.
- `processResources` takes the variant as a task input, so a cached task cannot hand back the wrong content set.

## Fixed

- `DanceRegistry.find()` answered any unknown `activeDance` with the bundled dance — a 147-frame animation with no frames on disk in a content-less build. It now falls back to the first installed pack, then to `none`.
- `MusicManager.resolveTrackForDance()` returned `default` when nothing matched, so a content-less build logged a failed load on every trigger; it now reports no track and playback stops with `no track available`.
- The **K** menu crashed with `IndexOutOfBoundsException` while building the Music or Dance pane on a machine with no tracks or packs; **Play preview**, **Preview dance on close** and **Position dance** are greyed out in that state instead.
- `triggerDance()` recorded its cooldown before it knew a dance existed, so with no pack installed a trigger burned the cooldown on an animation that could not draw.

## Installation

- **Minecraft:** Java Edition 1.21.11
- **Loader:** Fabric 0.18.1
- **API:** Fabric API 0.141.5+1.21.11
- **Client-side only**; not required on the server

Download `specialist-dance-1.21.11-fabric-1.6.1.jar` (2 038 434 bytes) for the mod plus its bundled dance and track, or `specialist-dance-1.21.11-fabric_lite-1.6.1.jar` (538 601 bytes) for the mod only — then put your own frames and music where the **K** menu tells you. Both need Fabric API.

Verify a download against these SHA-256 digests:

```
full  aea25e43365686ad2ece6c8ab40fa28777d29de8d7c6d15d9fd7b9b3e07fe1fc
lite  ff001bcdd82582de1432861ecac8f878419de80efff8b45fae20386051d7f9c4
```

## Known limitations

- PNG is the only loadable frame format — `NativeImage.read` rejects anything without a PNG header, so GIF, JPEG and WebP must be converted first with `tools/GifToFrames.java`.
- Pack folders and files must be lowercase with no spaces (`frame_000.png`, …).
- Ogg Opus and ALAC music are not supported.
- In the lite jar the name `specialist` is still reserved for the bundled dance, so a pack called `specialist` is not listed.
- `modVariant` is not validated: a typo such as `-PmodVariant=ligt` builds a full-content jar with the wrong name.
- Not yet observed in a running game: the lite jar loaded from a real `mods/` folder, the no-content **K** menu (the folder hints, the three greyed buttons, `no dance pack available, trigger skipped`), and any `pickup` activation line in a log.

releases.notes:
# Specialist Dance 1.6.0 — Your Rules + Animation Speed

The dance now fires on rules you write instead of a hardcoded ore list. Tell it which block you mine, which item you pick up, which mob you kill or which container you open, and it dances when that happens. The animation also plays faster or slower from the **K** menu, and **Mod Menu** opens the settings screen so you no longer need to know the keybind.

## Added

- `rules` in the config file — a list of `{trigger, source, item, enabled}` entries that replaces the built-in ore → drop map. Triggers are `mined` (this block yields this item), `pickup` (this item from anywhere), `mob` (this mob drops it) and `container` (this block gives it to you). A file with no `rules` key starts from the ten ore presets.
- **Your rules** screen on the **Rules** pane — a **Trigger** selector, **Source** and **Item** fields with TAB autocomplete that matches the part after the `:`, and **Pick mob** / **Pick block** / **Pick item** grids paged over the live registries.
- **Undo** and **Redo** in **Your rules** (`Ctrl/Cmd+Z` and `Ctrl/Cmd+Y`), 40 steps deep, covering add, delete, toggle, clear and reset.
- **Animation speed** slider in the **K** menu (`animationSpeed`), from `0.1x` to `10.0x` — a GIF that imports too slow can be sped up without touching its `pack.json`.
- `speedMultiplier` in `pack.json`, so one pack can carry its own playback speed. It overrides the global slider rather than multiplying with it, matching how `frameDurationMs` already overrides the global timing.
- `configVersion` in the config file with a `migrate()` hook that runs on load; the stamp is `4` in this release. A file written before the key existed is detected as version `0` and stamped current.
- Mod Menu integration — the mod's **Config** button in **Mods** opens the existing settings screen. Mod Menu is recommended, never required.

## Changed

- The **K** menu is two panes — a sidebar of **Music**, **Dance**, **Animation**, **Rules** and **Content** beside one column of rows. The music and dance pickers are scrollable lists of the real files in `config/specialist-dance/`, replacing the duplicate **Music track** dropdown, and the **Dance** pane previews the selected pack live.
- The ore list on the **Rules** pane became a rule editor — each row carries its own enable box, the source's item icon and both ids; left-click toggles, right-click deletes.
- Every numeric config field now has an upper bound as well as a lower one, so a stray extra zero (`frameDurationMs: 50000`) is clamped instead of hanging the trigger pipeline; an `animationEndBehavior` outside `stop`/`hold`/`loop` falls back to `stop`.
- Frame timing rounds instead of truncating, and floors at 1 ms, so a fast multiplier cannot divide a duration down to zero.
- The trigger diagnostic logs the frame duration the animation actually uses (after the speed multiplier) and also logs `speed`.
- `SpecialistDanceConfig` moved to `com.sebas.specialistdance.config`; your config file path is unchanged.

## Fixed

- Ids containing `_` are accepted again. Every vanilla id with an underscore was rejected, so the ten preset ore rules were deleted on every launch and a `mob` or `container` rule could never be saved.
- A rejected rule names the field it wants (`mob id must look like minecraft:zombie`) instead of one generic block-id message, and the red notice clears when you type, pick or delete.
- The **Trigger** row shows `mine`, `pickup`, `kill` and `open` instead of echoing the raw value back as `Trigger: mob`.

## Installation

- **Minecraft:** Java Edition 1.21.11
- **Loader:** Fabric 0.18.1
- **API:** Fabric API 0.141.5+1.21.11
- **Client-side only**; not required on the server

Download `specialist-dance-1.6.0.jar` (2 037 464 bytes) and place it in your `mods/` folder.

Verify the download against its published digest:

```
sha256  62dce6e659adcc6622078ef36df1330058ac35c4ae6c5e6f4b5f8945d55d0f59
```

releases.notes:
# Specialist Dance 1.5.0 — Animation Control + Dance Packages

The dance now respects the music's end, and raw GIFs can be imported directly in-game. You can hold the last frame, loop until the track finishes, or clear the overlay when the animation ends. Drop a GIF in the dances folder and the mod converts it to a playable pack with its own timing and audio.

## Added

- `stop`, `hold` and `loop` animation end behaviors are consumed by the HUD — `stop` plays one pass and clears the overlay, `hold` keeps the last frame, `loop` wraps around until the music ends.
- `MusicManager.isPlaying()`, so the animation can tell when its track has finished instead of guessing from a timer.
- One diagnostic line when a dance ends, naming the reason, the configured behavior, `musicEnabled` and whether music was driving the end (`debug: true`).
- Drop a `.gif` into `config/specialist-dance/dances/` and press **Rescan** — the mod composites the GIF frames, writes a `frame_NNN.png` pack, reads the GIF's frame delay into `pack.json`, and treats the result as a new dance.
- Optional sidecar files next to a dropped GIF — `<name>.ogg` (or another supported audio format) and `<name>.json` (copied as `pack.json`).
- `pack.json` with `frameDurationMs` and `track` — per-pack timing overrides the global `frameDurationMs`, and a pack's own audio is used while the track selector is on `default`.
- Pack audio appears in the music selector as `<pack>/<track>`.
- New dance packs open the **Position dance** editor once, both at startup and after **Rescan**. The list of packs already shown is persisted in `seenDances`; on upgrade, packs already in the folder are marked seen so they do not all pop at once.
- **Fit** now uses the current frame's aspect ratio, and the layout editor previews the middle frame instead of a possibly blank frame 0.

## Changed

- With `musicEnabled: false`, or when no audio device is available, there is no end signal for `hold` and `loop`, so both fall back to `stop` — one finite pass — instead of cancelling on the first frame.
- World change, player death, an invalid pack and a missing frame now end the animation through the same path, which also stops the music.
- An invalid dance pack says why — unreadable, no `frame_NNN.png` files, or a frame run with gaps — instead of the same silent `-1` for all three.
- **Rescan** releases cached pack textures so a replaced GIF or pack reloads.
- **Play preview** in the K menu plays the track the active pack would use, including its own audio, instead of always previewing the global selection.
- A `pack.json` larger than 1 MB is ignored; the pack still plays with the global timing. Unsupported pack audio formats (`.opus`, `.m4a`, …) are logged and skipped instead of failing silently.
- A pack folder named `specialist` is rejected because it would shadow the bundled dance.

## Fixed

- `hold` and `loop` with music off drew nothing at all; the animation was cancelled while rendering frame 0.
- Raw `.gif` files in the dances root were ignored by the scanner.

## Installation

- **Minecraft:** Java Edition 1.21.11
- **Loader:** Fabric 0.18.1
- **API:** Fabric API 0.141.5+1.21.11
- **Client-side only**; not required on the server

Download `specialist-dance-1.5.0.jar` (1 993 562 bytes) and place it in your `mods/` folder.

Verify the download against its published digest:

```
sha256  7f2b670cdb64aaa090309820482fb53f8f3a7010e25a5cc84b720e77571bc0b9
```

This jar bundles the `specialist` dance (147 frames) and the `default` track.

## Known limitations

- PNG is the only loadable frame format — `NativeImage.read` rejects anything without a PNG header, so GIF, JPEG and WebP must be converted first (the mod does this automatically for dropped GIFs).
- Pack folders and files must be lowercase with no spaces (`frame_000.png`, …).
- Ogg Opus and ALAC music are not supported.
- GIF decode runs on the render thread — importing a large GIF may freeze the game briefly.

# Specialist Dance 1.4.0 — Dance Packs + Layout

Your own dance frames, and control over where the animation appears. A folder of PNGs becomes a selectable dance, and the result can be positioned and resized in-game.

## Added

- User dance packs from `.minecraft/config/specialist-dance/dances/<name>/` — a folder of `frame_000.png … frame_NNN.png` becomes a selectable dance.
- `activeDance` config field and a **Dance pack** selector in the **K** menu.
- **Position dance** screen — drag the animation anywhere, scroll to zoom, with **Center**, **Fit** and reset buttons; the choice is saved on close.
- **Open music folder** and **Open dances folder** buttons in the **K** menu, so custom content is one click away.
- **Rescan** button — picks up music files and dance packs added since launch without restarting the game.
- **Preview dance on close** button in the config screen.
- `tools/GifToFrames.java`, which converts an animated GIF into a dance pack.

## Changed

- The frame count is detected per pack instead of hardcoded to 147.
- The config screen lays out every row from a computed cursor, so the dance controls no longer collide with **Done** at short window heights.
- Animation end behaviors renamed to `stop`, `hold` and `loop`, all of which clear when the music stops; the old `loop-until-music-ends` migrates to `loop`.

## Fixed

- Dance frames now scale to the stage instead of cropping the top-left corner.
- Dance frames draw at their true aspect ratio — the bundled `specialist` frames (498×351) had been stretched into a square box since v1.0.0.
- Text colors use ARGB so they render correctly in 1.21.11.
- MP3, FLAC and WAV tracks no longer upload an empty OpenAL buffer, which played back silently.
- The animation is cleared on world change and on death.

## Installation

- **Minecraft:** Java Edition 1.21.11

- Pack folders and files must be lowercase with no spaces (`frame_000.png`, …).

Custom music now supports more common formats. The bundled track and existing `.ogg` files still work the same way.

## Changed

- Custom music supports Ogg Vorbis, WAV, AIFF (`.aiff`/`.aif`), AU, MP3 and FLAC files.
- Java Sound decoders (`javasound-mp3`, `javasound-flac`) are bundled via jar-in-jar for wider format support.

releases.notes:
## Specialist Dance 1.3.0 — Sound On

Dance music is here. When a dance triggers, the selected track plays and stops with the animation.

### Added

- Dance-triggered music with a bundled `default` Ogg Vorbis track.
- Music settings screen opened with **K** — enable/disable music, adjust volume, select a track, preview it, and stop playback.
- Custom music support from `.minecraft/config/specialist-dance/music/`. Filenames become track names and `default` is reserved for the bundled track.
- `musicEnabled`, `musicVolume`, and `musicTrack` config fields.
- Fallback to the bundled `default` track when the selected custom track is missing or cannot be loaded.

### Changed

- Music restores the previous OpenAL context after playback and shutdown instead of clearing it.
- Buffer loading and shutdown now guard OpenAL context and object IDs.

### Fixed

- Shutdown no longer clears Minecraft's active OpenAL context.
- Tracks with more than two channels are downmixed to stereo for playback.

### Installation

- Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11
- Fabric Loader 0.18.1
- Fabric API 0.141.5+1.21.11
- Client-side only; not required on the server

Download `specialist-dance-1.3.0.jar` and place it in your `mods/` folder.

### Known limitations

Custom music currently supports Ogg Vorbis only. Ogg Opus, MP3, WAV, FLAC, and ALAC are not supported yet. Files added while the game is running are not picked up until the next launch.

releases.notes:
## What's new

The big one: the dance is now **origin-aware**. It only plays when you mine a valuable ore and pick up the drop from that ore.

Before, any diamond pickup counted — a chest, a trade, a mob, or loot lying on the ground would all fire the animation. Now each broken ore remembers its position, the drop that comes out of it gets linked back to that ore, and only a pickup of *that* item triggers the dance.

### Changed

- The trigger is origin-aware — chests, trades, mobs and pre-existing ground items no longer trigger the dance.
- Diagnostic logging is now gated behind `"debug": true` in the config.

### Added

- Pickup detection via a Mixin on `ClientPacketListener.handleTakeItemEntity` (local player only, matched by entity id).
- `config/specialist-dance.json` — enabled/debug toggles, association timeouts and radius, and animation duration/size/position/cooldown.

### Fixed

- Drop association now reads the item stack on a later client tick, because the spawn packet arrives before the item data. Without this, drops were misidentified as stone, dirt and the like.

## Tracked ores

| Ore | Drop |
|---|---|
| Diamond Ore / Deepslate Diamond Ore | Diamond |
| Emerald Ore / Deepslate Emerald Ore | Emerald |
| Gold Ore / Deepslate Gold Ore | Raw Gold |
| Nether Gold Ore | Gold Nugget |
| Iron Ore / Deepslate Iron Ore | Raw Iron |
| Ancient Debris | Ancient Debris |

## Install

1. Install Fabric Loader for 1.21.11 and [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).
2. Drop `specialist-dance-1.2.0.jar` into your `mods/` folder.

Client-side only — the server doesn't need it. Full config reference in the [README](https://github.com/Sebasjgg27/specialist-dance-mc#configuration).
